findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition removes 5-arg overload
findings.body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first. Any existing caller using the max_width,max_height form (4-5 arguments) will now either raise ArgumentError or have max_height misinterpreted as opts hash. The resize wrapper was correctly migrated to a dimensions string, but downsize needs a single method handling both forms or distinct names.

findings.title: In-place downsize overwrites source and ignores failure
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) using the same path for source and destination and discards the boolean return value. If convert/gifsicle fails (convert_with returns false and logs only), the original upload file can be truncated or corrupted, yet the loop continues and Upload.create_for proceeds with the damaged file. Use a separate temp file, check the return value, and abort on failure instead of overwriting in place.

findings.title: Client max size hardcoded to 10MB ignoring site settings
findings.body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js lines 182 and 246 replace Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. This breaks admin configuration: attachments still need max_attachment_size_kb enforcement (server does not downsize non-images), and sites with max_image_size_kb larger than 10MB will have valid uploads incorrectly rejected client-side while sites with smaller limits will allow uploads that then rely on server downsizing. Restore per-type site-setting lookup.

findings.title: Downsize loop mishandles SVG and animated GIFs
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 64 only checks FileHelper.is_image?(filename) before downsizing. For SVG this will rasterize/alter a vector image via ImageMagick convert, unlike OptimizedImage.create_for which special-cases .svg with a plain copy. For animated GIFs it passes dimensions "80%" to downsize_instructions_animated which delegates to gifsicle --resize-fit, an option that expects WxH geometry not a percentage, so conversion will fail every retry. Skip SVG and pass valid GIF geometry or use gifsicle --scale.
